<h2 class="section-title">India Markets</h2>

<ul class="digest-points">
  <li><strong>Market surge on oil relief:</strong> The Sensex and Nifty rallied over 550 points in early trade, supported by a 5% decline in crude oil prices following a pause in US-Iran tensions.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi_?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I6</a> <a href="https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi__?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I8</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I13</a></span></li>
  <li><strong>Forex inflows and rupee stability:</strong> RBI’s strategic measures, including FCNR(B) schemes, have successfully attracted nearly $32 billion in inflows, providing critical support to the rupee and potentially paving the way for up to $85 billion in total inflows.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I1</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I3</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I5</a></span></li>
  <li><strong>Corporate debt activity:</strong> UltraTech Cement is planning a significant Rs 5,000 crore rupee bond issuance, signaling robust corporate credit demand ahead of the upcoming RBI policy meeting.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">I9</a></span></li>
</ul>

<h2 class="section-title">Global Cues</h2>

<ul class="digest-points">
  <li><strong>Geopolitical cooling and market outlook:</strong> The easing of Middle East tensions and the subsequent drop in Brent crude are driving a rally in Indian bonds and equities, with investors now shifting focus to the upcoming US Federal Reserve meeting and domestic Q1 earnings.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxPREo0N0gwZF9WbndhVmxycGFteHdsa2ZEQ1BCUV85TVdKLTRfdlBYb0tlQnY4SzNCdHh2dEloR2k4QWFuYlNYazRucHZGa1dxOHNNdGYzcmo1M1BEUExzZGlBMm45WUJHTU1RYUxOZ3RvT2w2MU1yTUpWQUthRzdOLUJ0bHVBeHJLSmNYcVZkS3F6eVplb0NSelcxek54UXkxaHd4QXVzRWIyRVBVczEzbUhETHZzOTIyZWtHdEt3?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W2</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W3</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W4</a></span></li>
  <li><strong>Monetary policy expectations:</strong> Market consensus suggests the RBI will likely maintain a status quo on the repo rate during the August MPC meeting, balancing inflation concerns with the recent volatility in energy prices.<span class="source-chips"><a href="https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiygFBVV95cUxOSjNaMGVJUGN5YzFZcEtsQVZmdGphdjlya1ZYa1hWa3RNNTdOZnlaV2lwWTRsVWIxNGVxckt1bC1xbGc0ZjVyVHZDVjFCYUNOVjk4dk16MUwxWlk1YmZzQUFLWTVua0cweE52VDQydGRUSkpqSGRIdGowZzBaUHFfbS1UQ2l5SHd4SVJ1REpaNVlrVGhSUlE4dTRSRzB3VUlxMlVjaEtjeFVuS1NtbjMwb1Q3elF0SUpxWHlHczh4NzItcjF3d0N4VW1B?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W5</a> <a href="https://news.google.?oc=5&amp;hl=en-US&amp;gl=US&amp;ceid=US%3Aen" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W6</a></span></li>
